identity.what_it_is: A 15.2-hectare (38-acre) city-operated sand beach and park on Toronto's Lake Ontario waterfront, the largest beach in Toronto.
identity.where: Beaches neighbourhood, Toronto, Ontario, Canada, at the foot of Woodbine Avenue, south of Lake Shore Boulevard, next to Ashbridge's Bay and Kew-Balmy Beach.
identity.warnings: The harvested source set includes several pages about Woodbine RACECOURSE (a horse-racing track that opened in 1956; see F30) — a different Toronto landmark that only shares the name 'Woodbine.' Do not conflate it with this beach. Two toronto.ca facility-listing pages and blueflag.ca returned only JS-shell navigation with no usable beach facts.

spike_candidates.statement: One family has held exclusive, bid-free rights to sell food and alcohol on Woodbine Beach for 20+ years, renewed by council for 20 more.
spike_candidates.tension: Toronto's busiest public beach has had its only food concession locked up by one family for decades because council keeps renewing it without a competitive bid.

spike_candidates.statement: Only 10 of Woodbine's roughly 95 sand volleyball courts are public; the other 85 require a paid Ontario Volleyball Association membership.
spike_candidates.tension: The public beach's signature activity is mostly gated behind a private membership fee, not open recreation.

spike_candidates.statement: A 2008 master plan promised a $17M promenade turning Woodbine into a world-class waterfront park, but it had no funding or council approval.
spike_candidates.tension: A grand public vision for the beach stalled indefinitely for lack of money, and no source confirms it was ever built.

facts.fact: Woodbine Beach, on the Lake Ontario waterfront, is the largest beach in Toronto.
facts.quote: woodbine beach is situated along toronto waterfront 's with lake ontario and is the largest beach in toronto.

facts.fact: Woodbine Beach Park covers 15.2 hectares (38 acres) and was created in 1950.
facts.quote: area 15.2 hectares (38 acres) created 1950

facts.fact: Before Lake Shore Boulevard was extended to Woodbine Avenue in the 1950s, the area was a wooded area nicknamed 'the cut' rather than a bathing beach.
facts.quote: until lake shore boulevard was extended to woodbine avenue in the 1950s, woodbine beach was not a bathing beach, but rather a wooded area known as 'the cut'.

facts.fact: Woodbine Beach and Kew-Balmy Beach have been Blue Flag certified for cleanliness and swimming suitability since 2005.
facts.quote: woodbine beach and kew-balmy beach are blue flag certified for cleanliness and are suitable for swimming, with this distinction being awarded to woodbine since 2005.

facts.fact: Water and sand quality at the beach has improved dramatically since 1990, with daily water testing and daily machine-grooming of the sand.
facts.quote: since 1990, the quality of the water and sand has improved dramatically.

facts.fact: Water temperature at the beach can be unpredictable, occasionally dropping to the lower teens Celsius due to wind-driven upwelling of cold deep-lake water, regardless of air temperature.
facts.quote: occasionally water temperature can drop to the lower teens celsius for days, due to upward swirl of chilly deep-lake water known as upwelling, which is driven by strong westerly wind

facts.fact: Woodbine Beach and neighbouring Ashbridge's Bay are a popular spot to watch Victoria Day fireworks.
facts.quote: woodbine beach and neighbouring ashbridge's bay are a popular place to visit to see the fireworks for victoria day.

facts.fact: The beach offers rentals of bicycles, canoes, kayaks and standup paddleboards alongside its 90-plus volleyball courts.
facts.quote: there are over 90 volleyball courts, and various outdoor leisure activity rentals, such as bicycles, canoes, kayaks, and standup paddle boards.

facts.fact: The Donald D. Summerville Outdoor Olympic Pool next to the beach began construction in 1961 and was designed with temporary scaffolding for spectator seating in case Toronto ever hosted the Olympics.
facts.quote: construction for the pool started in 1961, and it was designed to add temporary scaffolding for the spectator seats in the event toronto was to ever host the olympics.

facts.fact: The Martin Goodman Trail, a waterfront multi-use path, runs along the boardwalk parallel to the shoreline at Woodbine Beach.
facts.quote: the martin goodman trail runs along the boardwalk.

facts.fact: George Foulidis and his family held exclusive rights to sell food and alcohol on Woodbine and the eastern beaches for 20 years, and city council renewed the rights without competitive bidding for 20 more years around 2007.
facts.quote: exclusive rights to sell food and alcohol on woodbine and the eastern beaches have been held by george foulidis and his family for 20 years. three years ago bussin spearheaded a successful vote at city council to renew it without competitive bids for 20 more years.

facts.fact: As of 2010 the only restaurant at the beach was the Boardwalk Pub, charging $11 for gourmet burgers and fries.
facts.quote: the only restaurant at the beach is the dated boardwalk pub in the parking lot on lake shore blvd. east, with a menu featuring food and prices you would expect at a tourist attraction: gourmet burgers and fries for $11

facts.fact: Only 10 of Woodbine's sand volleyball courts are public; the other 85 are run by the Ontario Volleyball Association and require a membership starting at $45 for the summer.
facts.quote: there are 10 public volleyball courts in the sand at woodbine beach. the other 85 are operated by the ontario volleyball association, and you must be a member to play. adult league memberships start at $45 for the summer.

facts.fact: The Balmy Beach Club sits on a half-hectare of land donated to the people of the beach by a resident in 1875.
facts.quote: the balmy beach club itself sits on a half-hectare of land, donated to the people of the beach by a resident in 1875.

facts.fact: The city runs a boathouse at Balmy Beach where a few owners store canoes and kayaks for $80 a year.
facts.quote: the city runs a boathouse on balmy beach, staffed by city employees. a few lucky owners store their canoes and kayaks there - sometimes for years without using them - at a cost of $80 a year.

facts.fact: There are 350 businesses in the Beach neighbourhood along Queen St. E., per the Beach Business Improvement Association's executive director.
facts.quote: there are 350 businesses in the area says deborah etsten, executive director of the beach business improvement association.

facts.fact: There are two off-leash dog areas at the eastern beaches, at the foot of Lee Ave. and at the foot of Nursewood Rd.
facts.quote: a fenced-off area at the foot of lee ave. is for off-leash dogs; so is a lovely, less populated strip of beach at the foot of nursewood road.

facts.fact: A 2008 Lake Ontario Park master plan for Waterfront Toronto envisioned a world-class public park with more than 37 kilometres of shoreline from Cherry Beach to the eastern beaches.
facts.quote: there are big plans for woodbine beach in the lake ontario park master plan, the vision for a world-class public park with more than 37 kilometres of shoreline stretching from cherry beach to the eastern beaches, prepared for waterfront toronto in 2008.

facts.fact: Building a promenade linking Ashbridge's Bay to Tommy Thompson Park under the master plan would cost approximately $17 million.
facts.quote: building the promenade would cost approximately $17 million, says gaffney

facts.fact: When a section of the Ashbridge's Bay boardwalk blew out in a 2008 storm, it took over a year to repair for lack of funding.
facts.quote: when a section of the ashbridge's bay boardwalk blew out in a storm in 2008, it took over a year to fix.

facts.fact: Despite thousands of visitors on busy weekends, the Woodbine bathing station has only eight bathroom stalls for women, even after a recent facelift.
facts.quote: despite a recent facelift, the woodbine bathing station has eight bathroom stalls for women.

facts.fact: The Star's 2010 beach profile lists average July water temperature at 15°C and the sand as extremely fine and calcareous over a limestone base.
facts.quote: average water temperature in july: 15c you'll be sitting on: sand that is extremely fine and calcareous over a limestone base, according to todd knapton of hutcheson sand and mixes.

facts.fact: There is one public parking lot at Woodbine Beach on Lake Shore Blvd. East, with free or low-rate parking that is hard to find on warm evenings or sunny weekends.
facts.quote: there is one public parking lot at woodbine beach on lake shore blvd. east, which offers free parking or low rates, depending on the time and day.

facts.fact: Woodbine is the gateway to three kilometres of sandy waterfront stretching east to the R.C. Harris Water Treatment Plant, with Kew-Balmy Beach in between.
facts.quote: this beach is also the gateway to three kilometres of glorious, sandy waterfront stretching eastward to the art deco palace that is the r.c. harris water plant, with kew-balmy beaches in between.

facts.fact: On summer weekends the 92 Woodbine bus and 501 Queen streetcar are packed, and the Ashbridges Bay Park parking lots fill up by 10 a.m.
facts.quote: on any given summer weekend, expect the 92 woodbine bus and the 501 queen streetcar to be packed, and the parking lots at ashbridges bay park fill up by 10 a.m.

facts.fact: Lifeguards are present at the beach throughout the summer.
facts.quote: there are lifeguards present throughout the summer.

facts.fact: The beach periodically carries an unpleasant smell from a nearby sewage treatment plant when the wind blows the wrong way.
facts.quote: if there is a flaw in woodbine beach's shiny veneer, it's the periodic smell from the nearby sewage treatment plant.

facts.fact: The Donald D. Summerville Outdoor Olympic Pool complex includes a five-metre diving board into the Olympic-size pool.
facts.quote: the donald d. summerville outdoor olympic pool complex lets you dive from a five-metre board into the olympic-size pool.

facts.fact: Woodbine Beach sits at approximately 43.66°N, 79.31°W in Toronto, Ontario.
Woodbine Racecourse, a horse-racing track that opened in Toronto in 1956, is a separate landmark that only shares the 'Woodbine' name with this beach.
facts.quote: woodbine racecourse stands as a beacon of canada's horse racing heritage, tracing its origins back to 1956 when it first opened its gates in toronto.

facts.fact: Strong west-to-east winds along Lake Ontario's north shore are the condition that drives upwelling events, the mechanism cited for Woodbine's unpredictable water temperatures.
facts.quote: strong winds from the west to the east are ideal for upwellings to occur.

facts.fact: Brandon Pitts opened Prana Coffee Bar on Queen St. E., across from a Starbucks, as of the 2010 Star profile.
facts.quote: brandon pitts, who just opened prana coffee bar, a gourmet coffee shop across the street from a starbucks on queen st. e.

facts.fact: Local councillor Sandra Bussin, who represents Ward 32 Beaches-East York, recalled a predecessor's warning against changing the beach.
facts.quote: the former councillor said to me: 'don't entertain too much change on the beach. people won't accept it,'

facts.fact: Woodbine Beach, together with Kew-Balmy Beach and Balmy Beach Park, formed the eastern shoreline of 'old Toronto.'
facts.quote: woodbine beach, together with kew balmy beach and balmy beach park, formed the eastern shoreline of old toronto.

facts.fact: Woodbine has a rowdier, busier vibe than calmer Toronto beaches like Sunnyside or Cherry Beach.
facts.quote: unlike the serene oases on the toronto islands, or the less-frequented beaches like sunnyside or cherry beach, it's a rowdier vibe here.

facts.fact: As of the 2010 Star profile, visitors could not rent a boat, canoe, bicycle, rollerblades, or even a sun parasol at Woodbine Beach.
facts.quote: you can't rent a boat, canoe, bicycle, rollerblades, or even a sun parasol to sit under at woodbine beach.

recency.newest_item: BlogTO's July 2019 profile is the newest substantive report on beach conditions, confirming Woodbine remains Blue Flag certified 'year after year' with lifeguards present all summer (the Wikipedia article was last edited July 2026 but is an encyclopedia entry, not a fresh field report).

conflicts: Wikipedia (F08) says the beach offers bicycle, canoe, kayak and paddleboard rentals; the Toronto Star's 2010 on-the-ground profile (F36) says none of those rentals existed at the time — likely reflects services added since 2010, but no source confirms when.

Wikipedia says water 'around 20c' is often experienced July-September (F06), while the Star's 2010 vitals box lists average July water temperature as 15c (F22) — a roughly 5-degree discrepancy with no reconciling source.

derivations.fact: 2010-07 (Star profile publication) minus 'three years ago' = 2007 council vote renewing the Foulidis family's food/alcohol concession without competitive bid for 20 more years
10 public courts + 85 OVA-run courts = 95 total sand volleyball courts at Woodbine Beach
